value: Limited to compound numbers from 21 to 50.
The et forms 21, 31, 41, and 51 are never hyphenated.

evidence.notes: The summary and common trap state the et versus hyphen rule for this number range.

value: Excludes verbs with irregular future stems and verbs with spelling changes.
For -re verbs the final e must be dropped before the endings are added.

evidence.notes: The exceptions list irregular stems and spelling changes; the common trap notes the -re e drop.

value: The -s of quatre-vingts is dropped when another number follows.
71 (soixante et onze) uses et instead of a hyphen.

evidence.notes: The conditions, exceptions, and common traps give both restrictions.

value: premier/première and dernier/dernière are the only irregular ordinal forms.
The feminine of premier is première, never premier.

evidence.notes: The exceptions list the two irregular pairs and the common trap states the feminine form.

proposals.entity_key: Formation of passé simple for regular -er verbs
value: Limited to regular -er verbs; -cer and -ger verbs have spelling changes before endings starting with -a.
The -âmes and -âtes endings carry a circumflex.

evidence.notes: The exceptions and common traps give the spelling-change and circumflex limits.

proposals.entity_key: Formation of passé simple for regular -ir and -re verbs
value: Limited to regular -ir and -re verbs.
The -îmes and -îtes endings carry a circumflex.

evidence.notes: The common trap notes the circumflex on -îmes and -îtes.

value: en must not be omitted before the present participle.
The gerund has no subject of its own; it shares the subject of the main clause.

evidence.notes: The common trap requires en; the shared-subject property follows from the gerund construction.

value: The correct auxiliary (avoir or être) must be chosen.
Compound-tense agreement rules apply to the past participle.

evidence.notes: The agreement rules and common trap state the auxiliary choice and the agreement requirement.

value: The auxiliary must be the same one used in the passé composé.
The dependent clause action must be anterior to the main clause action, and être requires participle agreement.

evidence.notes: The condition, explanation, and common trap give the anteriority and auxiliary limits.

value: The auxiliary must be in the imparfait, not the present.
The past participle agrees with the subject when être is the auxiliary.

evidence.notes: The common trap and agreement rule give the tense and agreement limits.
